title: Seqlen-driven kernel metamapper and exploration schedule
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight "metamapper" service that predicts, per-model and per-request shape (seq_len, batch_size, attention-type, sparse/dense), the best kernel implementation family and a short horizon exploration schedule. The metamapper is a regression+uncertainty model (small ensemble) that outputs: preferred kernel variant, expected latency/cost delta vs baseline, and an exploration budget (percent of traffic and probe cadence). This ticket covers the runtime integration, low-overhead microprobe scheduling, and an initial rollout plan for canary and automatic fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Metamapper model is trained offline on existing kernel benchmark traces and integrated behind a feature flag in the runtime.
Runtime routes 100% of a canary group to metamapper decisions with probe budget enabled and records probe outcomes in telemetry.
Observed p95 latency change for the canary is within +/- 8ms of baseline and tokens/sec improves by >= 4% for targeted heavy-tailed seq_len workloads.
When model uncertainty > configured threshold, runtime automatically applies conservative fallback (stable kernel) and marks requests for additional probing.
All experiment decisions, kernel switches, and probe outcomes are emitted as structured events and visible on the Console rollout dashboard.
No regression in memory peak or KV cache hit-rate beyond 2% compared to baseline over a 24h canary window.
implementation_plan: 1) Offline: build dataset extractor that aggregates per-model, per-batch-shape microbenchmarks from internal infra traces and lab runs (use 50k samples covering seq_len 4..8192).
2) Train: prototype a compact metamapper (random forest + quantile regressor OR small MLP with MC dropout) that predicts latency and uncertainty; produce exportable artifact.
3) Runtime sidecar: add metamapper client that (a) receives request shape metadata, (b) returns kernel plan & probe schedule, (c) logs decisions.
4) Microprobe scheduler: implement non-blocking probe path that runs <1% of requests through alternate kernels using background streams and reports latency/cost.
5) Rollout: feature flag + canary group (5% traffic) -> observe 24h -> expand to 25% if metrics stable -> automatic fallback on regressions.
6) Console integration: add per-model metamapper decision heatmap and probe coverage metrics to rollout dashboard.
7) Cleanup: remove debug flags, finalize telemetry retention and alerting for kernel regressions.
benchmarks_and_metrics: Primary metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens_per_second, cost_per_1M_tokens, kernel-switch overhead (ms), memory_peak (GB), KV_cache_hit_rate.
Baselines: current stable kernel family per model and the prefill/decode split policies measured across standard bench harness (repo: github.com/redwood/runtime-benchmarks).
Datasets: synthetic seq_len distributions (chatty short, docs long-tail) and 3 customer anonymized traces (PII scrubbed) for validation.
Target improvements: >=4% TPS for long-tail workload, no more than 5% regressions on short-seq latency p50, cost per token neutral or better.
Experiment probes: maximum 2% additional GPU cycles budgeted for probing in steady state; must be throttled during peak.
notes_and_decisions: We decided not to use a full bandit architecture for initial launch to keep runtime complexity low; instead use scheduled microprobes and uncertainty-driven gating.
Model format: export as ONNX and load in the lightweight metamapper service to avoid introducing Python in hot path of runtime.
Probe execution should prefer batched probe windows to amortize kernel switch cost; single-request probes are allowed only if the request is already on a slow path.
Edge-case: for extremely long seq_len > 4096, metamapper by default picks largest-memory-optimized kernel; explicit probe only if uncertainty high and budget allows.
comments: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Ticket created. Initial scope covers model, runtime sidecar, microprobe scheduling, and Console metrics. See design doc linked.
2026-03-03 Marcus Li: Pushed prototype metamapper (onnx) and small synthetic bench. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4127.
2026-03-07 QA: Live lab runs show 6% TPS uplift on long-tail but a 3ms p95 regression on short chatty tests—investigating probe cadence.
2026-03-10 Data: Added customer trace with heavy doc workloads; metamapper uncertainty remains high for mixed-batch shapes—plan to add batch_shape feature.
2026-03-14 Marcus Li: Implemented throttle for probes during peak util; preparing canary rollout to 5% tomorrow.
risk_mitigation: Conservative defaults: metamapper disabled by default per-tenant; require opt-in or canary before enabling in production.
Auto-fallback on any 10-minute window with > 5% p95 regression; heartbeat checks to disable probing if memory pressure observed.
Telemetry: add a synthetic canary that runs every 5m to detect silent regressions from kernel selection changes.
